subject: Packaging options & stepwise upgrade plan for Lumen Health
messages:
From: Devin Marshall <devin@lumenhealth.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Initial: Packaging options for inference pilot

Connor —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're putting together the requirements for a 3-month inference pilot (clinical summarization + triage reranking) and want to make sure our procurement asks are aligned with Redwood's packaging.

Attached is a short requirements spreadsheet (Lumen_Pilot_Requirements.xlsx). A few questions up front:
- Can we start on a compact plan and burst to higher throughput when needed?
- What does a clean upgrade path look like from compact -> reserved/dedicated, both technically and on billing?
- Are there any stepwise discounts if we commit to a 12-month conversion after pilot?

Our procurement timeline is tight — aim to finish vendor selection by 2026-11-12. Happy to hop on a short call mid-next week.

Thanks,
Devin Marshall
Head of Automation Programs
Lumen Health

Attachment: Lumen_Pilot_Requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet, 12KB)

From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
To: Devin Marshall <devin@lumenhealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-26T10:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial: Packaging options for inference pilot

Hi Devin —

Appreciate the requirements doc. Quick answers up front, then a suggested two-track approach so your procurement can compare outcomes:

Options (summary):
1) Compact pilot -> throughput lift (self-serve hosted API start)
   - Start on Compact tier (metered tokens, prefix caching enabled). Low friction, fast onboarding.
   - Burst capacity available (subject to regional availability); bursts billed at metered rate + short burst addon.
   - Upgrade path: when you hit a sustained throughput threshold we convert to Reserved capacity (Dedicated). Workload state (models, KV caches) can be migrated with minimal interruption.

2) Throughput-first pilot -> reserved commit
   - Provision a small Dedicated pool for pilot months 1–3 (predictable latency).
   - If you convert to a 12-month reserved commit, we credit pilot months against the first-year commitment and provide a structured discount.

Pricing note (high level):
- Compact pilot: nominal setup, pay-as-you-go token rate.
- Dedicated conversion: typical conversion credit = pilot spend credited against committed minimum; discount ranges depend on term and capacity. See attached pricing matrix for sample scenarios.

I'll attach the Redwood_Pricing_Matrix_v3.xlsx which maps typical commitments to discount tiers and conversion credits. If you can share an expected token/day or QPS for the pilot, I can map it to concrete numbers.

Next steps:
- Can we do a 30-minute procurement + engineering sync on 2026-11-02 or 2026-11-03?
- I'll propose a mutual action plan (MAP) with timelines and a draft SOW after that call.

Connor O'Brien
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
connor@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0128

Attachment: Redwood_Pricing_Matrix_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet, 48KB)

From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-10-28T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Packaging options — internal alignment (pricing & concessions)

Team — forwarding Devin's reqs and my reply. Procurement will push on discount + guaranteed ramp. Quick thoughts so we're aligned if Devin asks for a steeper concession: 

- Floor concession: 15% first-year discount on committed Dedicated if they convert within 90 days of pilot end; pilot spend to be credited up to 50% of month 1 commitment.
- Upside: 18% if they commit to an SLA (we'll require a 6-week provisioning notice for Dedicated ramp).
- Product constraint: we can allow compact->burst for up to X QPS but need to flag KV cache cold-start on fast bursts; include a small migration window (we can script warm-up).

My ask: Ben/Kim — can you confirm finance ok with 15% floor and an approval path for 18% with SLA? Lauren — can you prepare a short SOW outline that references conversion credits and a 12-month term?

Thanks,
Connor

Connor —

Thanks for the clear options. Procurement reviewed internally and came back with two asks:
1) We need a stronger first-year concession — they're requesting 20% off committed Dedicated for year one if we convert after pilot.
2) A formal assurance that we can scale from Compact -> Dedicated within 14 days once we signal ramp (our ops windows are tight).

To be transparent, Lumen prefers to start on Compact (lower initial spend) but wants contractual certainty around fast conversion and predictable billing once we scale.

Can you share a draft SOW and example amendment language that honors a 14-day conversion SLA (or a good-faith timeline + escalation path)? Also, procurement wants the MAP by 2026-11-12.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Devin

Devin —

Thanks for the clarity. We can accommodate both asks with a short set of commitments and a MAP that outlines conversion economics. High-level proposal below (I'll attach a draft SOW and the MAP PDF):

Proposal (pilot + conversion):
- Pilot: 3 months on Compact tier (metered). Minimal setup.
- Conversion option: Option to convert to Dedicated within the pilot window or within 14 days after pilot completion. We commit to a 14-calendar-day conversion SLA for capacity provisioning (subject to region capacity at time of signal).
- Financials: 18% first-year discount on committed Dedicated spend if Lumen converts within 30 days of pilot end. Pilot spend credited against first-month commitment up to 60% (reduces cash due at conversion).
- Escalation: If regional capacity prevents 14-day provisioning, we provide burst credits and a prioritized provisioning queue + weekly roll-up until Dedicated is live.

Why 18%? It balances procurement's desire for a meaningful concession and Redwood's need to preserve margin on short-notice provisioning. If you need 20% we can entertain it for a 24-month committed term — happy to discuss.

Attached: SOW-draft.pdf, MAP-Lumen-LM0789.pdf (MAP contains milestone dates and DocuSign links). I'll circulate a formal MAP to procurement and the HubSpot deal after you confirm this approach.

Next steps suggested:
- Lumen: confirm which conversion window you prefer (30-day with 18% or 24-month term for 20%).
- I'll send the DocuSign envelope with the MAP + SOW for your internal routing once you confirm.
- Schedule deconflict call: 2026-11-12 at 10:00 AM PT (procurement + engineering + Redwood).

Connor O'Brien
